label: Main crops
title: Main crop in each parish
subtitle: The crop with the largest area, USDA Cropland Data Layer 2024

rank.note: Ranked by the area of each parish's main crop, in acres.

how: Each parish is coloured by the crop with the largest mapped area in 2024. Click a parish for its other main crops. Grass and pasture are left out, because they are not crops. A parish with under 100 acres of crops has no main crop.
limits: The Cropland Data Layer is a satellite map made once a year by USDA. Its accuracy is highest for the large crops (rice, soybeans, corn, cotton, sugarcane) and lower for small ones. NASS publishes accuracy tables for each year.
Each parish is the total of 30 m pixels inside it for 2024. A pixel can be wrongly labelled, and double crops (for example wheat then soybeans) count for both crops.
These are the crops mapped in one year. They are not a list of what a given farm grows and do not show rotations.
The most recent year is the last one NASS has published, so it is usually the previous growing season.
The main crop is the one with the most acres, even if it leads by a small margin. Check the table in the pop-up.

credits.text: Crop maps: USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service, Cropland Data Layer 2024, summarised by parish with the CropScape service (George Mason University)
Parish boundaries: US Census Bureau cartographic boundary files (public domain)
